title: Should animals be kept in zoos?
speaker: BBC Learning English

keywords.def: the protection of plants, animals and the natural world from damage done by humans
not willing, and therefore hesitant, to do something
(idiom) used to emphasise that an activity needs two people who are willing to be actively involved for it to succeed
different from what would normally be expected, in a bad way
repeated, purposeless behaviour performed by captive animals in response to the stress of being confined, including pacing, head-bobbing and swaying

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 这里是BBC学习英语的6分钟英语节目。

sentences.en: I'm Neil. And I'm Georgie. In this programme we're discussing a controversial topic that often produces strong feelings: should animals be kept in zoos?
sentences.zh: 我是尼尔。我是乔治。在本期节目中，我们将讨论一个经常引发强烈情感的争议话题：动物应不应该被关在动物园里？

sentences.en: What's your opinion on this debate, Neil?
sentences.zh: 尼尔，你对这场辩论有什么看法？

sentences.en: Oh, it's a really difficult question, Georgie.
sentences.zh: 哦，这是一个非常棘手的问题，乔治。

sentences.en: I think there are good scientific reasons for having animals in zoos, but also, it seems to me a little bit sad and cruel for wild animals to be locked up.
sentences.zh: 我认为把动物养在动物园里有很好的科学理由，但同时，对于野生动物来说，被关起来似乎又有点悲伤和残酷。

sentences.en: For some, zoos are a good way to teach people about nature and save endangered species from extinction.
sentences.zh: 对某些人来说，动物园是向人们普及自然知识以及从灭绝边缘拯救濒危物种的好方法。

sentences.en: Others think separating animals from their natural habitat is cruel and unnecessary.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则认为将动物与其自然栖息地隔离是残酷且不必要的。

sentences.en: Either way, with an estimated 700 million visitors every year, zoos remain popular – but are they a good thing?
sentences.zh: 无论如何，每年估计有7亿游客，动物园依然很受欢迎——但它们真的是一件好事吗？

sentences.en: We'll be debating the pros and cons, as well as learning some useful new words and phrases.
sentences.zh: 我们将辩论正反两方的观点，并学习一些有用的新词汇和短语。

sentences.en: And remember you can find all the vocabulary for this programme on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.
sentences.zh: 请记住，你可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到本节目的所有词汇。

sentences.en: Now, I have a question for you, Georgie.
sentences.zh: 现在，我有一个问题要问你，乔治。

sentences.en: In 2022, five animals escaped from Sydney's Taronga Zoo in Australia, but were the escaped animals: a) elephants b) lions c) zebras Hmm.
sentences.zh: 2022年，有五只动物从澳大利亚悉尼的塔龙加动物园逃脱，这些逃跑的动物是：a) 大象 b) 狮子 c) 斑马 嗯。

sentences.en: I can imagine zebras running away from the zoo.
sentences.zh: 我能想象斑马从动物园逃跑的画面。

sentences.en: Neil Education is the primary reason that zoos give for why they should exist.
sentences.zh: 尼尔，教育是动物园认为它们应该存在的首要原因。

sentences.en: The fact is school children all over the world are often bussed to zoos.
sentences.zh: 事实是，世界各地的学童经常坐大巴去动物园。

sentences.en: I remember myself going to see lowland gorillas at Zoo Atlanta every single year, and the point of this was to introduce us to conservation.
sentences.zh: 我记得自己每年都去亚特兰大动物园看低地大猩猩，这样做的目的就是为了让我们了解自然保护。

sentences.en: One argument for keeping animals in zoos is to educate people about the importance of conservation: the protection of plants, animals and the natural world from human damage.
sentences.zh: 支持将动物养在动物园的一个论点是，教育人们认识自然保护的重要性：保护植物、动物和自然世界免受人类的破坏。

sentences.en: A second point is that zoos often invest in research programmes that help endangered animals.
sentences.zh: 第二点是，动物园经常投资于帮助濒危动物的研究项目。

sentences.en: Now as we know, pandas are notoriously reluctant to mate: the female pandas have a narrow window of fertility, they're solitary creatures and it takes two to tango when it comes to reproduction.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，大熊猫向来不愿意交配：雌性大熊猫的受孕期很短，它们是独居动物，而且在繁殖这件事上需要双方共同努力。

sentences.en: But a lot of money in zoos – it goes to, sort of, find ways to encourage these animals to mate.
sentences.zh: 但是动物园里的大量资金都用于寻找某种方法来鼓励这些动物交配。

sentences.en: A second argument is that zoos protect endangered species from extinction through breeding.
sentences.zh: 第二个论点是，动物园通过繁育来保护濒危物种免于灭绝。

sentences.en: William mentions pandas, animals which are reluctant, meaning slow and unwilling, to reproduce.
sentences.zh: 威廉提到了大熊猫，这种动物不愿意繁殖，也就是行动迟缓、不情愿繁殖。

sentences.en: Male and female pandas need a little help to make babies, and zoos can provide this help.
sentences.zh: 雄性和雌性大熊猫需要一点帮助来生宝宝，而动物园可以提供这种帮助。

sentences.en: William uses the idiom, it takes two to tango, to describe an activity which needs two people, or in this case two pandas, to be willing to make something a success.
sentences.zh: 威廉使用了习语“巴掌拍不响”（需要双方配合），来描述一项需要两个人，或者在本案中需要两只熊猫愿意配合才能取得成功的活动。

sentences.en: Now, let's turn to some of the arguments against zoos with Nikita Dhawan, a 19-year-old animal-rights activist from India, who spoke to BBC World Service programme, What in the World: I don't think zoos should exist for several reasons, the first one being zoos' detrimental impact on both the physical and psychological health of animals.
sentences.zh: 现在，让我们转向一些反对动物园的观点，采访对象是来自印度的19岁动物权利活动家尼基塔·达万，她接受了BBC世界频道节目《环球扫描》的采访：我认为动物园不应该存在，原因有几个，首先是动物园对动物身心健康的负面影响。

sentences.en: Many studies and research have shown that many animals in zoos and aquariums display abnormal behaviours like head-bobbing, pacing, stereotypical behaviours, signs of mental distress.
sentences.zh: 许多研究表明，动物园和水族馆里的许多动物会表现出异常行为，如反复点头、踱步、刻板行为以及精神痛苦的迹象。

sentences.en: The second reason, I would say, is that zoos cannot mimic the natural habitat of animals in the wild.
sentences.zh: 我要说的第二个原因是，动物园无法模仿野生动物在自然界中的栖息地。

sentences.en: Nikita argues that being enclosed in a zoo is so stressful for wild animals it leads to abnormal behaviour: behaviour that is different, and worse, from what would normally be expected.
sentences.zh: 尼基塔认为，被关在动物园里对野生动物来说压力极大，导致了异常行为：这种行为与正常预期不同，且更糟糕。

sentences.en: Examples of this include animals pacing their cages in circles and rocking, bar-biting, and even self-harm.
sentences.zh: 这方面的例子包括动物在笼子里转圈踱步、摇晃、咬栏杆，甚至自残。

sentences.en: And they're so common in captive animals, there's a name for it: zoochosis.
sentences.zh: 这些在圈养动物中如此普遍，以至于有一个专有名词：动物园精神病。

sentences.en: Even zoos with large enclosures cannot fully mimic, or copy, the natural habitats and open spaces these animals would enjoy in the wild.
sentences.zh: 即使是拥有大型围场的动物园也无法完全模仿或复制这些动物在野外所享受的自然栖息地和开阔空间。

sentences.en: And imagine how a polar bear, evolved for life in the frozen Arctic, would feel, trapped in a zoo in a much warmer country.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，一只为冰冻北极的生活进化而来的北极熊，被困在一个气候温暖得多的国家的动物园里，会有什么感觉。

sentences.en: Some zoologists have compared zoochosis to human traumas like post-traumatic stress disorder but say it's even more damaging.
sentences.zh: 一些动物学家将动物园精神病与人类创伤（如创伤后应激障碍）进行比较，但表示它的危害更大。

sentences.en: For captive animals, everything – including the air they breathe – is traumatic.
sentences.zh: 对于圈养动物来说，一切——包括它们呼吸的空气——都是创伤性的。

sentences.en: We've heard a few arguments for and against keeping animals in zoos.
sentences.zh: 我们已经听取了关于是否将动物养在动物园的一些正反方观点。

sentences.en: What do you think, Neil? Have you changed your opinion at all?
sentences.zh: 你怎么看，尼尔？你改变看法了吗？

sentences.en: Well, I think there are really strong arguments on both sides, so I'm still not sure, Georgie.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为双方都有非常有力的论据，所以我还是不确定，乔治。

sentences.en: Well, we know how some of the animals at the Sydney Zoo felt about things because they managed to escape!
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们知道悉尼动物园的一些动物对这件事的感受，因为它们设法逃跑了！

sentences.en: But what was the answer to your question, Neil?
sentences.zh: 但是你那个问题的答案是什么，尼尔？

sentences.en: Well, Georgie, I asked you which animals escaped from a zoo in Sydney, Australia, in 2022.
sentences.zh: 嗯，乔治，我问过你2022年哪种动物从澳大利亚悉尼的动物园逃跑了。

sentences.en: Was it a) elephants, b) lions, or c) zebras?
sentences.zh: 是 a) 大象，b) 狮子，还是 c) 斑马？

sentences.en: And I said zebras. I'm afraid that was the wrong answer.
sentences.zh: 我说是斑马。恐怕我答错了。

sentences.en: It was actually lions – how scary! OK. It's time to recap the vocabulary we've learned.
sentences.zh: 其实是狮子——多吓人啊！好了。是时候回顾我们学过的词汇了。

sentences.en: Conservation is the protection of plants, animals and the natural world from human harm.
sentences.zh: 保护（Conservation）是指保护植物、动物和自然世界免受人类伤害。

sentences.en: If you are reluctant to do something, you don't want to do it, or you do it very slowly.
sentences.zh: 如果你对做某事感到不情愿（reluctant），说明你不想做，或者做得非常慢。

sentences.en: The idiom, it takes two to tango, refers to an activity which needs two people to willingly and actively take part for it to succeed.
sentences.zh: 习语“巴掌拍不响”（it takes two to tango），指的是需要两个人自愿并积极参与才能成功的活动。

sentences.en: The adjective, abnormal, means different from what would normally be expected, in a bad way.
sentences.zh: 形容词“异常的”（abnormal），指与正常预期不同，且是不好的方面。

sentences.en: Zoochosis is a term to describe the repeated, purposeless behaviour performed by captive animals in response to the stress of being confined, including pacing, head-bobbing and swaying.
sentences.zh: 动物园精神病（Zoochosis）是一个术语，用来描述圈养动物为了应对被关押的压力而表现出的重复、无目的的行为，包括踱步、点头和摇晃。

sentences.en: And finally, if you mimic somebody or something, you imitate it or copy it.
sentences.zh: 最后，如果你模仿（mimic）某人或某物，你就是在效仿或复制它。

sentences.en: Once again, our six minutes are up, but don't forget we have a worksheet and a quiz that you can use to practise the vocabulary from this episode.
sentences.zh: 我们的6分钟时间又到了，但别忘了我们有一份练习表和一个测验，你可以用来练习本期节目的词汇。

sentences.en: Visit bbclearningenglish.com. Goodbye for now.
sentences.zh: 访问 bbclearningenglish.com。再见。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
